{{short description|Mexican mathematician (born 1942)}}
{{family name hatnote| López de Medrano||lang=Spanish}}
'''Santiago López de Medrano Sánchez''' (born October 15, 1942, in [[Mexico City]]) is a Mexican mathematician, who works as a researcher at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM).<ref>[http://www.matem.unam.mx/fsd/santiago?set_language=en&cl=en Faculty profile], UNAM, retrieved 2014-12-19.</ref><ref name="elizondo">{{citation|title=Topology and Geometry: The Mathematics of Santiago López de Medrano|first=E. Javier|last=Elizondo|website=SMM 60th Anniversary|publisher=Mexican Mathematical Society|url=http://www.matmor.unam.mx/~muciray/smm/60/santiago.html|language=Spanish|accessdate=2014-12-19}}</ref> His research has concerned [[knot theory]], [[singularity theory]],  [[biomathematics]], and [[differential topology]].<ref name="elizondo"/>

López de Medrano did his undergraduate studies at UNAM,<ref name="elizondo"/> and earned his Ph.D. from [[Princeton University]] in 1969, under the supervision of [[William Browder (mathematician)|William Browder]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=1414|name=Santiago Sanchez Lopez de Medrano}}</ref> He returned to UNAM as a researcher and professor in 1968, and was president of the Mexican Mathematical Society from 1969 to 1973.<ref name="elizondo"/>

López de Medrano presented his work on [[knot invariant]]s at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1970.<ref name="elizondo"/>
In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2014-12-19.</ref>
